rem:q-beta-spectral-bridge-sketch:
Remark Argument sketch for the Q_β spectral bridge. Sketch.

Scope of the asymptotic expansion. Two sub-steps in the Taylor comparison are conditional: First, the order-h^2 term of \ln(V_{\mathrm{pp}}/V_{\mathrm{nn}}): the step z h + O(h^2) = \ln(1 + zh) + O(h^3) needs the h^2 coefficient to be -z^2/2, which is not computed. Second, the exponential remainder rests on conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay, a conjecture, so the remainder bound is conditional. The +1.31 keV residual and the CODATA 7\% agreement are empirical comparisons, not proof steps.

Form A side. The normal form counit reads \lvert\Delta(\mathrm{net})\rvert = h(2 - h)/2 = h - h^2/2 + O(h^3), obtained via direct expansion of the single-wrap symbolic closed form (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic).

Form B side. The Hecke perturbation carries the half-factor \Delta_\beta(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})\,\mathbb{I} = \tfrac{h}{2}\,\mathbb{I} (prop:beta-decay-transfer-matrix). The change in Markov-traced volume per generator incorporates this factor:

  \Delta \hat V_i
  \;=\;
  z\,(\Delta M_i)_{11} + (\Delta M_i)_{21}
  \;=\;
  \tfrac{z\,h}{2} + O(h^2).

At single wrap with A = 1, the proton-to-neutron conversion affects two generators, \sigma_0 and \sigma_1 (prop:neutron-qvalue-symbolic). The total log-ratio is:

  \ln\!\frac{V_{\mathrm{pp}}}{V_{\mathrm{nn}}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i \in \{0,1\}}
    \ln\!\frac{\hat V^{\mathrm{pp}}_i}{\hat V^{\mathrm{nn}}_i}
  \;\approx\;
  2 \cdot \tfrac{z\,h}{2}
  \;=\;
  z\,h \;+\; O(h^2)
  \;=\;
  \ln(1 + z\,h) + O(h^3).

Ratio. Form the dimensionless ratio \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}} / \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}} and divide by E_0 to cancel h in the leading term:

\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}}
&=
\frac{h - h^2/2 + O(h^3)}
     {(z h - z^2 h^2 / 2 + O(h^3))\,/\,z} \\
&=
\frac{h - h^2/2}{h - z h^2 / 2} \cdot \bigl(1 + O(h)\bigr) \\
&=
\frac{1 - h/2}{1 - z h/2} \cdot \bigl(1 + O(h)\bigr) \\
&= 1 + \tfrac{(z - 1)\,h}{2} + O(h^2).
\end{aligned}

The intermediate identity \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}}/E_0 \cdot z = z h - (z h)^2/2 + O(h^3) isolates the dimensional content of the 1/z factor. Form B requires z to normalize the eigenfunction basis to the Markov-traced volume. This does not mean that Form A and Form B measure different observables.

Exponential remainder. Both truncations inhabit the spectral decomposition of the q-Hamiltonian along the Gröbner basis filtration of the free-neutron sector K \subset H_3(q) at q = q_0. Following conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay, each finite-depth truncation \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(N)} incurs an error bounded by C(K) \cdot e^{-c(K) N}, where C, c > 0 are structural constants. At N = 0, this yields the observed +1.31 keV residual. At N \geq 1, the bound is sub-keV.

The bridge formula:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{A}}
  \;=\;
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\mathrm{B}} \cdot \bigl(1 + \tfrac{(z-1)\,h}{2} + O(h^2)\bigr)

demonstrates that Form A and Form B represent a single observable in two bases: the normal form counit basis (where \Delta(\mathrm{net}) is discrete) and the transfer-matrix basis (where \ln V_{\mathrm{pp}}/V_{\mathrm{nn}} is the natural eigenfunction). The 1/z factor in Form B is the required Markov–Jones normalization mapping the eigenfunction space onto MeV.

The exponential-remainder bound dampens the eigenfunction (conj:archimedean-remainder-exponential-decay), so finite-depth truncations converge exponentially fast in depth N.   1. G(q,z) is symmetric and G[0,0] = 1, for every z.

  \det G(q,z) \;=\; -\,\frac{(z-q)^5\,(qz+1)^5\,\bigl((q^2+1)z - q^3\bigr)\,

rem:q-holonomy-locality-derivation:
Remark Derivation: locality from flatness of the KZ connection.

Locality from flatness of the KZ connection

The lifted-crossing locality hypothesis reduces to a statement about the holonomy of the Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection at generic q. Cross-talk between two lifted crossings measures the curvature of a flat connection. Flatness implies factorization.

Setup — the KZ connection

Let X_n be the configuration space of n distinct complex points. The quantum KZ connection on X_n is flat. The monodromy representation coincides with the quantum-group R-matrix representation.

Applying to the mass endomorphism

Model each crossing of an atomic braid as a puncture in X_n. A lifted crossing inserts \Phi_q(z_c); an unlifted crossing inserts the identity. The mass contribution is the trace of the braid-word operator, computed via parallel transport.

Claim. At generic q, the parallel transport factorizes over disjoint punctures:

  \mathrm{Tr}\!\left[
    \prod_{c \in S} \Phi_q(z_c) \cdot \rho(\beta)
  \right]
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Tr}[\rho(\beta)] \cdot \prod_{c \in S}
  \eta(c),

where \eta(c) is the single-crossing expectation value.

Proof sketch. By flatness, closed loops encircling separated subsets have commuting holonomies. Simultaneous diagonalization decomposes the trace. The \Phi_q insertions act by scalar on each eigenstrand. Thus, the multi-crossing expectation is a product of single-crossing expectations. The scalar obstruction requires non-abelian monodromy, which flatness rules out. \square

Failure of flatness

Flatness is equivalent to semisimplicity of the braided tensor category. At generic q, representations are semisimple and locality holds. At roots of unity, non-semisimple subquotients appear and locality fails.

The aether as the locality window

The KZ connection is flat at every level (the infinitesimal braid relations are homogeneous), so flatness does not single out the pinned parameter q_0 \approx 1.11; what does is that q_0 is not a root of unity, so the monodromy target H_n(q_0) is semisimple and the locality statement is about the generic Hecke representation. The soft confinement level is far from the first non-trivial root of unity, so locality holds to high order.

Corollary — exponential mass scaling

Combining locality with the crossing-graded expansion gives, at the homogeneous fixed point, \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{K}; q_0) = \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\mathcal{K}) \cdot (1 + \xi(q_0))^{c(\mathcal{K})}. Each crossing multiplies mass by \approx 94. Exponential scaling is the empirical signature of KZ flatness at the aether.

  \sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_\ell}^{\epsilon_\ell}

The Jones polynomial of K and of its time-reversed counterpart K^T coincide. The operator T is an involution (T^2 = \mathrm{id}). It preserves q, color-sheet flavors, and Hecke generator signs. It acts purely on the ordering of crossings.

For a braid word \beta, define \beta^T as the reversed word. Trace cyclicity gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta^T). conj:p-from-braid-mirror:
Conjecture Parity P as mirror reflection of the braid diagram (writhe sign flip). Within the QOU framework, parity P acts as the mirror reflection of the braid diagram — each positive crossing \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} and vice versa, with the q-parameter held fixed (q \mapsto q, not q \mapsto q^{-1}). Equivalently, P negates the signed writhe w(K) \mapsto -w(K) of every braid word. P is an involution (P^2 = \mathrm{id}) and is distinct from:

  • the bar-involution Bar-involution and its P_{\mathrm{avg}} / P_{\mathrm{skew}} projections, which acts as q \mapsto q^{-1} AND \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} simultaneously (= composite CPT);

The action

For a braid word \beta = \sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_\ell}^{\epsilon_\ell} in B_n (or its image in H_n(q)):

  P \;:\;
  \sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k}
  \;\longmapsto\;
  \sigma_{i_k}^{-\epsilon_k}
  \qquad (q\text{ held fixed}).

On the writhe, this gives w(P\beta) = -w(\beta) — a sign flip on the bar-anti-symmetric writhe quantity classified in bar-involution-table3-data.

Disentangling parity from CPT

The composite bar-involution acts as both:

  (\text{bar}) \;:\;
  \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1},
  \qquad
  q \mapsto q^{-1}.

This is CPT composed: bar = P \cdot C \cdot T in the natural order, where:

Acts on Symbol map
Hecke generator chirality only \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, q fixed (= P alone)
Color sheets only flavor u \leftrightarrow \bar u (= C alone)
Markov trace cyclicity only braid word reversal (= T alone)

P alone (this conjecture) corresponds to the first row only — it fixes q, fixes color-sheet flavors, and fixes trace cyclicity; it only mirrors the diagram. Composed with C and T, it recovers the bar-involution.

  • GB filtration level: ℓ-dependent per-atom (P preserves Coxeter length but flips signs of generators).
  • Jet order: h^0 (P fixes q; no q-deformation parameter enters the P action).
  • Bar-symmetry status: bar-trivial (P does not act on q; bar-involution acts on q AND \sigma_i, so P alone is a strict sub-action).

Writhe w(K) (the observable that P negates) is classified in bar-involution-table3-data as bar-anti-symmetric, consistent: bar reverses writhe via the composite P \cdot C \cdot T, of which P is the writhe-acting factor.

Scope at the Hecke-letter level

P as written is a map on braid words, not on H_n(q). The conjecture defines P by \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} with q held fixed. On the braid group B_n this is an involution. It does not descend to the Hecke algebra: an algebra map of H_n(q) that is linear over the scalars and sends a generator to its inverse forces 2(q - q^{-1}) = 0, so it exists only when q^2 = 1 in characteristic other than 2. The reason is that \sigma_i^{-1} satisfies the Hecke relation at the parameter q^{-1}, not at q.

What does descend. Let P_+ and P_- be the idempotents of \sigma_i for its eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}, and let e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 with mirror e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}, as in the Breit–Wheeler vertex. Three involutions send a letter to a letter, and they form a Klein four-group.

  • The mirror \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} together with q \mapsto q^{-1} is the bar involution on a letter. It keeps P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to e^+. Its profile is that of C, or of CT if q \mapsto q^{-1} is read as antilinear.
  • The map \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1} keeps q, exchanges P_+ and P_-, and sends e^- to -e^+. Its profile is that of CP.
  • The map \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i together with q \mapsto q^{-1} exchanges P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to -e^-. It is the only one of the three with the profile of P. It is not linear over the scalars unless q^2 = 1, and q \mapsto q^{-1} has no counterpart at the real aether value q_0.

The bar involution as composite CPT. At the letter level the bar involution keeps both eigenlines. A map with the profile of CPT would exchange them, as P does. So the factorisation bar = P \cdot C \cdot T in the summary below is not supported at the letter level, where bar has the profile of C (or CT).

Item 1 below. Multiplying (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 by \sigma_i^{-2} gives (\sigma_i^{-1})^2 = (q^{-1} - q)\,\sigma_i^{-1} + 1, which is the Hecke relation at q^{-1}. The quadratic at q is therefore not preserved by P with q fixed.

The conjecture asserts an involution P on braid-group elements (P^2 = \mathrm{id}) sending each Hecke generator \sigma_i to \sigma_i^{-1}, fixing q, and such that the bar-involution factors as P \circ C \circ T.

  1. Invariance of the Hecke quadratic under P. The quadratic is preserved (since both \sigma_i and \sigma_i^{-1} satisfy the same relation): the quadratic (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 is invariant under P because (\sigma_i^{-1} - q)(\sigma_i^{-1} + q^{-1}) = 0 also holds (multiply the original by \sigma_i^{-2}).

conj:type-b-folding-cpt:
Conjecture Type-B Coxeter folding realises CPT via Hecke-algebra \mathbb{Z}/2 fixed points. The involution \iota: s_i \leftrightarrow s_{n-i} of the Coxeter diagram folds the Weyl group S_n into a Coxeter group of type \mathrm{B}_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} (of type \mathrm{A}_1 at n = 3), and the canonical atomic-braid Hecke algebra H_n(q) folds to the Hecke algebra of that group with the weight function below, in Lusztig's quasisplit sense [lusztig2003, Sec. 16.2]. The folded algebra carries the bar involution and canonical basis of this weight function, and its GS normal forms are bar-involution invariant by construction. Stable matter = the elements of H_n(q) fixed by the algebra involution \theta(\sigma_i) = \sigma_{n-i} that lifts \iota; antimatter = the elements \theta moves. Under this folding, the composite CPT operator decomposes naturally as a tensor of:

  • C from color-sheet flavor conjugation
  • P from Type-B Coxeter folding, in role only: the fold \theta permutes the letters and keeps their eigenvalues, so it does not have the profile of P defined below
  • T from Markov-trace cyclicity

Type-B folding provides an alternative categorical realisation where the role of "P (braid mirror)" is replaced by "the Coxeter-fold Z/2", and the bar-invariance emerges from the folded Hecke algebra rather than from explicit \sigma_{i} \leftrightarrow \sigma_{i}^{-1} braid manipulation. The Type-B folding view is more compact but requires more category theory.

Rank and generator weights. The statement is made at the level of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras for every n. For odd n = 2m+1 the corresponding fold of the \mathfrak{sl}_n Cartan datum would put the adjacent roots \alpha_m, \alpha_{m+1} in one orbit, so the conjecture makes no claim about Cartan data. The rank is the number of \iota-orbits on the n-1 simple reflections, which is \lfloor n/2 \rfloor. At the level of Coxeter groups this is Lusztig's quasisplit case: with s_i the simple reflection of \alpha_i, the \iota-fixed subgroup of S_n is a Coxeter group generated by the longest elements of the \iota-orbits, and the folded Hecke algebra carries the weight function given by their ambient lengths [lusztig2003, Sec. 16.2]. The two parities differ only at the middle of the diagram. For even n the middle root \alpha_{n/2} is fixed, so its generator s_{n/2} has weight 1; the other generators s_i s_{n-i} have weight 2. For odd n = 2m+1 the middle roots \alpha_m and \alpha_{m+1} are adjacent and form one orbit, so its generator is s_m s_{m+1} s_m of weight 3; at n = 3 this is the whole folded group, of type \mathrm{A}_1. For n \ge 4 the weights are unequal, so the folded algebra is a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters. With the ambient parameter equal to q, as for H_n(q), these are q^2 on the generators s_i s_{n-i} and q or q^3 on the middle generator. The fold is not an algebra map that sends each folded generator to the product of its ambient generators: for a swapped pair, \sigma_i \sigma_{n-i} has the three eigenvalues q^2, -1 and q^{-2}, while a Hecke generator of weight 2 has two.

On the type-B side the Markov traces are classified: there is exactly one for each parameter z and each sequence (y_k)_{k\ge 1} of values on the elements t_0't_1'\cdots t_{k-1}', and each restricts to Ocneanu's trace on the type-A subalgebra [geck-lambropoulou-2004, Def. 4.1, Thm. 4.3]. Which of these traces the T factor uses is not fixed by the conjecture.

Scope at fixed q. Three involutions send a Hecke letter \sigma_i to a letter: \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1} and \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i. They form a Klein four-group, the composite of any two being the third. Let P_+ and P_- be the idempotents of \sigma_i for its eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}, and let e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 with mirror e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}, as in the Breit–Wheeler vertex. The braid mirror \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} keeps P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to e^+, which is the profile of C (of CT if q \mapsto q^{-1} is read as antilinear). The map \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1} exchanges P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to -e^+, which is the profile of CP. Only \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i has the profile of P: it exchanges P_+ and P_- and sends e^- to -e^-.

Neither \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} nor \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i is realised by an algebra map of H_n(q) that is linear over the scalars, unless q^2 = 1.
